titulo_it: Voglio andare, voglio che tu vada

spero di.consejo: Construction with infinitive for the same subject.

texto: When you want something for yourself: **Voglio andare** (I want to go), **Spero di partire** (I hope to leave), **Penso di avere ragione** (I think I'm right). You don't say «voglio che io vada».
The **di**: **Penso di sapere la risposta** preposition is added with pensare and sperare.
When you want something for someone else: **Voglio che tu vada** (I want you to go), **Spero che lui parta** (I hope he comes out), **Penso che tu abbia ragione** (I think you're right).

frases.it: Voglio cambiare lavoro. Penso di cercare a Milano.
frases.es: Quiero cambiar de trabajo. Pienso buscar en Milán.
frases.en: I want to change work. I'm looking for Milan.

frases.it: Davvero? Io preferisco che tu resti qui a Roma con me.
frases.es: ¿De verdad? Yo prefiero que te quedes aquí en Roma conmigo.
frases.en: Really? I'd rather you stay here in Rome with me.

frases.it: Ma voglio che anche tu sia felice! Se trovo un buon posto, vieni anche tu.
frases.es: ¡Pero quiero que también tú seas feliz! Si encuentro un buen puesto, vienes tú también.
frases.en: But I want you to be happy too! If I find a good job, you come too.
analisis: If I find a good job

frases.it: Ci penserò. Spero di trovare una soluzione insieme.
frases.es: Lo pensaré. Espero encontrar una solución juntos.
frases.en: I'll think about it. I hope to find a solution together.

bloques.pregunta: Why does Luca say «penso di cercare» and not «penso che io cerchi»?

opciones.texto: Because the subject of the two verbs is the same (Luca thinks and Luca seeks).
opciones.explicacion: Mandatory rule: same subject requires «di» + infinitive preposition.

opciones.texto: Because «cercare» does not support subjunctive forms in Italian.
opciones.explicacion: Admit congiuntive when subjects are different.

opciones.texto: Because Milan is a destination set at this point of sign.
opciones.explicacion: The structure responds to the identity of grammatical subjects.

bloques.frase: Sara dice a Luca: «Io preferisco che tu ___ qui a Roma».

opciones.explicacion: Different subjects (Sara prefers / Luca stays): che + congiuntivo present.
The infinitive would only be possible if Sara were to stay («preferisco restare»).
«Resta» is present as an informal indication.

opciones.texto: Because there are two different subjects: «io voglio» and «tu sia».
opciones.explicacion: The change of agent between the main and the subordinate prayer requires congiuntive.

opciones.texto: Porque «felice» es un adjetivo que solo concierta con congiuntivo.
opciones.explicacion: The selection of the mode depends on the verb «volere» with double subject.

opciones.texto: Porque la frase expresa una acción pasada ya cumplida.
opciones.explicacion: It expresses a present desire projected towards the interlocutor.

bloques.pregunta: What does this daily statement express?
bloques.frase: Chiedo il permesso alla mamma prima di uscire.

opciones.texto: She's applying for mother's permission before she leaves the house.
opciones.explicacion: «Chiedere il permesso» is the usual placement to ask for permission.

opciones.texto: He gives a mandatory order to his mother to get her out.
opciones.explicacion: The subject requests permission to leave himself.

opciones.texto: That his mother completely forbids him from studying in the afternoon.
opciones.explicacion: It alludes to the procedure of asking for permission before leaving.

bloques.frase: Spero di trovare una buona soluzione per tutti
bloques.traduccion: I hope to find a good solution for all of us.

bloques.pregunta: How does «I hope you're coming.» (different subjects) translate?

opciones.explicacion: It would mean «I hope I come.» (same subject).
The «vieni» indicator does not meet the standard subordination standard.

bloques.frase: Marco spera ___ vincere la gara di corsa.

opciones.explicacion: With the same subject, «sperare» is linked with infinitive by the «di» preposition.
«Che» would require a later conjugated verb with express or tacit subject.
«Sperare» does not govern the «a» preposition to infinitive.

intro: A golden rule of the Italian: if the subject of the two verbs is the same, the infinitive is used; if the subjects are different, it is used «che + congiuntivo».
